name: FOXO4-DRI

track.title: Research use only
track.line: Not FDA approved; research labels not for humans

what.text: FOXO4-DRI is a lab-made peptide designed by a group at Erasmus University Medical Center in Rotterdam and published in 2017. It copies part of the FOXO4 protein, built in a “D-retro-inverso” (DRI) form, which the authors say can give peptides new chemical properties.

src.label: Baar et al., Cell, 2017 (full text, PMC)

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and cell studies:

items.text: Senescent cells are damaged cells that stop dividing but do not die. In them, the FOXO4 protein holds onto p53, a protein that can trigger cell death. FOXO4-DRI competes with FOXO4 for p53, which pushes p53 out of the nucleus and sets off cell death in senescent cells. Drugs that clear senescent cells are called senolytics.
In lab dishes, it lowered the survival of senescent human lung cells more than normal cells.

src.label: Baar et al., Cell, 2017 (full text, PMC)

items.text: A 2025 structural study found that FOXO4 and FOXO4-DRI bind a loose, unfolded part of p53.

what.text: None of these effects has been tested in people.

research.text: Human evidence: none. No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. Everything is mouse, rat or cell work, starting with one 2017 mouse study.
No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. PubMed lists 19 papers mentioning FOXO4-DRI, none giving it to people, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial.

research.title: Senescent cells, chemotherapy damage and ageing mice (Baar et al.)

facts.v: controlled animal studies, FOXO4-DRI against saline (PBS), plus cell experiments
mice given the chemotherapy drug doxorubicin; fast-ageing XpdTTD/TTD mice; naturally old mice (about 110 weeks)
5 mg/kg three times, every other day, into a vein or the belly
results measured up to 30 days after treatment
senescence markers, liver and kidney blood tests, fur density, activity, body weight

research.found: In the chemotherapy mice, it reduced a liver damage marker (AST) and weight loss. In fast-ageing and old mice, it reduced senescence markers and improved fur density, activity and kidney blood tests. In fast-ageing mice, the kidney tests used groups of 7 to 8 mice per treatment. The paper reports no lifespan data.

src.label: Baar et al., Cell, 2017 (full text, PMC)

items.text: in naturally old mice, it lowered senescence in testosterone-making Leydig cells and raised testosterone.
in naturally old mice, sperm quality and sperm production improved.
it removed senescent cells from human cartilage cells grown in the lab.

src.label: Huang et al., Front Bioeng Biotechnol, 2021

items.text: in mice prone to lung high blood pressure, clearing senescent cells with FOXO4-DRI or another senolytic worsened lung blood pressure and caused loss of lung blood-vessel cells.

research.text: Animal results have not been confirmed in people.

us.text: Not FDA-approved for any use. No FOXO4-DRI product appears in FDA’s drug approval database, and no trial is registered. Products labelled “research use only” are not for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. A search of Drugs@FDA found no match.

FDA says products marketed “for research use only” or otherwise not for human consumption “have not been evaluated for safety and should never be used by humans.” Such products may not be sold for human use: FDA says it acts against firms selling unapproved products.

after.text: FOXO4-DRI is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered elsewhere on the List and with no current approval by any government health regulator for human use. For 2027, WADA adds “peptides” to the examples in S0. The lists do not say whether FOXO4-DRI falls under S0.
Australia: FOXO4-DRI is not named in the Poisons Standard that took effect on October 1, 2026. The TGA’s product register was not checked.

side.text: There are no human safety data. No one has published a study giving FOXO4-DRI to people. One mouse study found harm from clearing senescent cells.

items.text: in mouse models of lung high blood pressure, FOXO4-DRI worsened lung blood pressure and removed lung blood-vessel cells. The authors say clearing senescent cells may worsen lung blood flow.
the 2017 study gave short courses (three doses) that the authors describe as well tolerated. No formal toxicity studies were found.

src.label: Baar et al., Cell, 2017 (full text, PMC)

items.text: Health Canada warns that unauthorized injectable peptides may hold too much, too little or none of the ingredient, or contaminants. It says a “research use only” label does not make them legal.

unconfirmed: UK (MHRA) status and Australia’s TGA register were not checked against the regulator’s own record.
surprises: FOXO4-DRI is promoted as a senolytic for ageing, but it has never been tested in people, and the original 2017 mouse study did not measure lifespan.
A 2023 mouse study found that clearing senescent cells with FOXO4-DRI worsened lung blood pressure.
